subtitle: Spectral Transient Shaper
tagline: Reshapes attack and sustain separately in every FFT bin, without crossover bands, then finishes the result with optional saturation, clipping, oversampling, and limiting.

body.lead: A conventional transient shaper moves the whole signal at once. TB Spectral Transient Shaper analyses the sound in 1025 frequency bins and decides, bin by bin, where transient energy should rise, where sustain should tighten, and where the sound should stay untouched.

body.p: `ATTACK GAIN` and `SUSTAIN GAIN` boost or cut the two branches, and each has its own release. SIMPLE mode uses one sensitivity across the spectrum; EQ mode gives the low, mid, and high regions their own sensitivity. Two analyzers show what is detected, the monitor lets you hear each branch or only the change, and an optional output chain adds saturation, a soft clipper, and a limiter.

ul: Attack and sustain shaping per FFT bin (1024-point FFT, 4× overlap), with no crossover bands
`ATTACK GAIN` and `SUSTAIN GAIN` from −24 to +24 dB, each with its own `RELEASE`

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Spectral Transient Shaper 1.4.1 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.0.2 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Spectral Transient Shaper on a drum, bass, guitar, vocal, or bus track. By default `ATTACK GAIN` is +4 dB, `SUSTAIN GAIN` is −2 dB, and both releases are 50 ms.
Leave `SHAPER` {{3}} on SIMPLE and play the track. Watch the ATTACK {{5}} and SUSTAIN {{6}} analyzers.
Raise `ATTACK GAIN` {{7}} for more punch, or lower it to soften hits. Shorter `RELEASE` {{8}} makes tighter, sharper transients.
Lower `SUSTAIN GAIN` {{9}} to dry up room tails and ring, or raise it for more body.
Switch on `DELTA` {{4}} to hear only what the processing changes, then switch it off again.
Match the level with `OUTPUT` {{15}} and compare with `BYPASS` {{2}}.

How quickly attack shaping returns to neutral. Short values make tighter, sharper transients.

SIMPLE uses one sensitivity value across the spectrum. EQ uses low shelf, bell, and high shelf sensitivity bands.
How readily each branch detects attack or sustain. Shown on the analyzers as the sensitivity curve and reference line.

body.p: In EQ mode, each branch has three detection bands: a low shelf, a bell, and a high shelf. Each band has a frequency, a sensitivity, and a Q, shown on the analyzer. Use them to detect, for example, kick attack in the lows and cymbal sustain in the highs separately.

What you listen to. NORMAL is both shaper branches; ATTACK and SUSTAIN apply only that branch. All three run through the same output chain.
Hear only the difference against the latency-aligned input. ATTACK with DELTA is what the attack branch adds.

note.text: The spectral analysis adds latency, which the plug-in reports to the host. Oversampling and limiter lookahead add more. BYPASS reports zero latency while it is on.

body.p: The preset browser holds factory and user presets. Selecting one replaces every parameter as a single undo step. The arrows step through the bank; hold one to keep stepping. Save stores the current settings as a user preset, and LOAD USER PRESET... opens a saved file. After a change, the name shows (Custom).

body.p: Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Punchier kick
recipes.use: More click and impact without more level.
steps: Monitor ATTACK with DELTA to hear only what is added.
Match OUTPUT before comparing with bypass.

recipes.title: Drier drum room
recipes.use: Shorter room tails on overheads or a drum bus.
steps: Check in NORMAL that the cymbals still ring naturally.

recipes.title: Clearer consonants
recipes.use: Speech or vocals that need definition.
settings: Detect in the mid and high bands
steps: Use only the mid and high band sensitivity so the low end is not pumped.

recipes.title: Safe bus punch
recipes.use: Transient emphasis on a bus with peak safety.
steps: Keep the shaping small; the limiter only catches peaks.

Brought the latest attack and sustain graphs and the current spectral processing build to Windows VST3, and aligned the catalog, VST3, and installer versions at 1.4.1.

The EQ-mode analyzer and the processing now use the same sensitivity curve and reference line. Delta behaviour and latency are consistent across monitor sources, and the analyzer draws more efficiently.
